references.text: The concept of God's time: In John 2:4, Jesus says to his mother that 'my hour' has not yet come, a direct parallel expression to 'my time' (ὁ ἐμὸς καιρὸς) in John 7:8.

The fulfillment of the time: In John 8:20, it is emphasized that Jesus could not yet be seized, 'because his hour had not yet come,' confirming the theme that God's plan is governed by a specific time.

The transition from not-yet-come to come: In John 12:23, Jesus declares that 'the hour has come' for the Son of Man to be glorified, marking that the time which was 'not yet' in John 7:8 has now arrived.
The completion of the time: In John 13:1, it is stated that Jesus knew that 'his hour had come' to depart from this world, which is the final fulfillment of the time mentioned in John 7:8.
The hour has come: In John 17:1, Jesus asks the Father to glorify his Son, 'for the hour has come,' a direct reference to the time that was previously delayed in John 7:8.
